name: SeaVees
why: California canvas sneakers first sold in 1964 and relaunched in 2008, plus slip-ons and desert boots, with one store of its own in Santa Barbara.
origin: Launched by BFGoodrich in California in 1964; relaunched in 2008 by Steven Tiller.

craft_evidence.owned: NONE: no owned factory stated; uses long-standing partner factories in Vietnam
craft_evidence.makers: NONE: factories unnamed, "long-standing partner factories in Vietnam" only
craft_evidence.mills: NONE on product pages; LWG-certified tanneries mentioned unnamed
craft_evidence.madein: Brand-wide statement on help centre ("designed in California and responsibly made in Vietnam"); 0 of 1 product page sampled (Hayward Loafer) states a country; other product pages not sampled
craft_evidence.heritage: Dated and partly placed: 1964 BFGoodrich launch (no city), 1969 sold to Converse, closed 1971, original found in Tokyo 2005, relaunched 2008 (California)
craft_evidence.process: Partly: help centre says most styles are vulcanized (rubber foxing tape heat-pressed in an oven after stitching); materials listed per product page
craft_evidence.reasoning: States a country (Vietnam) and a vulcanizing process on the help centre, and a dated heritage story, but names no factory or mill and owns no facility; product pages carry no made-in line. Between 2 and 3 only on heritage; held at 2.

ownership.owner: Steven Tiller, its founder and CEO; Pentland Brands invested in 2017.
